name: Candy and confectionery (hard candy, caramels, imported/ethnic sweets)
native_basis_label: confection as placed on the market (as-sold solid)
scope_note: Covers hard candy, caramels, and imported/ethnic sweets (tamarind, chili, and similar). The dominant certifiable hazard is lead (adulteration + packaging + imported ethnic sweets), which binds the FDA 2006 candy guidance (0.1 ppm) with MERCOSUR/Paraguay concurrence at 100; total arsenic is likewise a real candy limit. Cocoa-containing confections route to the chocolate row. A confection with a Supplement Facts panel (e.g., supplement gummies) routes to Cat 16.

Pb.basis: candy as sold (binding candy ML; FDA 2006 candy guidance concurs at 0.1 ppm as US backstop)

Cd.rationale: Sugar confectionery (hard candy, caramels, chews) has no cadmium source: there is no cocoa and no soil-uptake plant tissue at the confection level. The documented cadmium contamination platform for this category is cocoa (certified under the chocolate row, which carries the EU cocoa-solids cadmium form_split). The known imported/ethnic-candy adulteration hazard is lead (and to a lesser extent arsenic), not cadmium. Rebuttable: if a routed source reports cadmium measured in a non-cocoa confection, re-adjudicate.
Cd.reference_method: Ingredient screen; cocoa-based confections route to the chocolate row.
Cd.regulatory_basis: No candy cadmium ML in any jurisdiction; cadmium pathway is cocoa (routed to chocolate)
Cd.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; Codex; FDA; MERCOSUR; Singapore; Paraguay

iAs.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for candy; the total-arsenic candy limit (MERCOSUR/Paraguay, 100 ug/kg) bounds the inorganic fraction (iAs <= tAs).
iAs.reference_method: Total-arsenic screen; no reflex inorganic-As speciation for candy.
iAs.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-As candy standard (100 ug/kg); no inorganic-As candy ML anywhere

tHg.rationale: Sugar, glucose syrup and confectionery fats carry no mercury source, and there is no bioaccumulation pathway in a candy. The 21 CFR 73.85 'Caramel; food use' mercury figure (100 ug/kg) is a purity specification for the caramel COLOUR ADDITIVE, not a limit for caramel candy, and is not applied here. Rebuttable if a routed source reports mercury in confectionery.
tHg.reference_method: No mercury pathway; screen on any novel ingredient.
tHg.regulatory_basis: No candy mercury ML anywhere; 21 CFR 73.85 is a colour-additive purity spec, not a food ML
tHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU; Codex; FDA (21 CFR 73 excluded as additive-purity); MERCOSUR

MeHg.rationale: No mercury source and no methylmercury formation pathway in sugar confectionery.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No methylmercury candy ML anywhere; no pathway

Ni.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a nickel maximum level for candy. A minor nickel pathway exists only where a confection contains hydrogenated fat (nickel is the hydrogenation catalyst); plain sugar/glucose confections carry none. Screened rather than dismissed so a hydrogenated-fat confection is caught.
Ni.reference_method: Nickel screen on any hydrogenated-fat-containing confection; no sovereign candy ML.
Ni.trigger: flag if the confection contains hydrogenated/partially-hydrogenated fat

Sn.rationale: No tin source in wrapped/boxed sugar confectionery; tin is a tinplate-can migration pathway only.
Sn.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); periodic ICP-MS tin verification.
Sn.regulatory_basis: No candy tin ML for non-canned product; canned-food 250 mg/kg limit applies to cans only

Al.rationale: Aluminium in confectionery derives from permitted aluminium-lake colour additives, not contamination, and is managed by additive law and by intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI, not by a per-food contaminant maximum level. No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant ML for candy.
Al.reference_method: Managed by additive law + TWI; periodic screen.
Al.regulatory_basis: Al managed by additive law (aluminium lakes) + TWI; no candy contaminant ML
Al.jurisdictions_checked: EU 1333/2008; FDA 21 CFR 73/74; Codex; JECFA/EFSA TWI

Cr.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium food maximum level (chromium(III) is an essential nutrient). Screened as the substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
Cr.reference_method: Total-chromium screen; substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
Cr.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation only if total chromium is anomalously elevated

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is reduced to chromium(III) in a reducing, sugar-rich confection matrix and is not stable as Cr(VI). No jurisdiction sets a Cr-VI food ML.
Cr-VI.reference_method: No routine Cr-VI speciation; reflex only on anomalously elevated total chromium.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No Cr-VI food ML anywhere; reduces to Cr-III in matrix

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; explicit-id lookup; legislated product-form splits preserved)
